$comment: RPC-SIGNATURE-DRIFT-GUARD-1 — the documented contract for .rpc() call sites
whose arguments (and sometimes the function name) cannot be resolved from the
TypeScript AST alone. The guard REFUSES to skip an unresolved caller silently:
every one must appear here, and every entry here must still match a real site.
file            — repo-relative path containing the unresolved call site(s).
unresolvedCount — EXACT number of unresolved sites in that file. A new one
changes the count and fails the guard, so widening an entry
is a deliberate, reviewable act rather than a silent drift.
rpcs            — every function the site can dispatch to. Each must exist in
the migrated database, and a statically-known function name
at the site must appear in this list.
reason          — why static resolution is impossible.
argumentCoverage— how the arguments ARE protected, since this guard cannot
Keep this list SHORT. Prefer making a call site statically resolvable over
adding an entry: a literal function name plus a literal argument object is
resultHandling — RPC-RETURN-CONTRACT-GUARD-1: how the RESULT of a dynamic call is checked, since a generic cannot be applied to a runtime-selected function name.

unresolvedCallers.reason: a local `rpc(fn, params)` helper forwards a function-name PARAMETER to admin.rpc(), so no single function name exists at the call site
unresolvedCallers.argumentCoverage: the suite executes every one of these RPCs against the real local database in db-ci's billing group; a stale argument name fails there as a live PostgREST error, not silently
unresolvedCallers.resultHandling: the helper returns the raw PostgREST envelope and each call site asserts the exact jsonb fields it expects (ok/reason/used/limit/reserved); those assertions run for real against the local database in db-ci's billing group

unresolvedCallers.reason: the argument object spreads a `params` function parameter over its literal base keys, so the full key set is only known at runtime
unresolvedCallers.argumentCoverage: the literal base keys cover every REQUIRED argument, and the suite calls the RPC for real in db-ci's security group
unresolvedCallers.resultHandling: the rows are asserted field by field (bucket_start/group_key/runs/succeeded/failed) against seeded fixtures in db-ci's security group
